about: Weather numbers come from official climate normals (IMD, DHM, the UAE's National Center of Meteorology), each with its source and checked date: a place's own 'source', or a month's 'src', a key in 'sources'. Never add a month we have no numbers for. Items can carry 'for' wording and 'picks_for' picks for women and men; the page shows the everyone wording without JS.
rules: Day clothes follow the warmest day of the month and evening clothes the coldest night, across the places we list. Where a guide gives only a range (Manali), day clothes follow the middle of the range. Shoes follow the night band when it is below 5 °C, else the day band. Rain of rain.min_mm or more in a month adds the rain extras, unless snow is possible; a snow note adds the snow extras.

places.name: Manali
more: What to wear in Manali in December

snow.dec: Possible from December to February, but not every year
snow.jan: Possible from December to February, but not every year

places.note: The weather can turn from warm to snowy within minutes, so carry warm layers every day. Himachal Tourism says nights can fall below −5 °C.

source.label: Incredible India's ranges, as given in our Manali guide

snow_note.mar: Snowfall is mostly from December to early March, so early March can still bring snow

places.name: Shimla

snow.dec: Possible, usually from late December. More likely in January and February
snow.jan: More likely in January and February than in December
snow.feb: More likely in January and February than in December

places.note: Some nights are far colder than the average, usually clear nights just after snow.

source.label: IMD Shimla averages (1971–2000)

snow_note.mar: Sometimes: IMD counts about 1 to 2 snow days in an average March (1990–2010)

places.name: Kashmir

snow.dec: Gulmarg often gets snow in December, but some early winters are dry

places.note: Chillai Kalan, the 40 coldest days of the Kashmir winter, starts on 21 December. Lakes and taps can freeze.

source.label: IMD averages for Srinagar and Gulmarg (1981–2010)

notes.oct: Gulmarg is much colder than Srinagar, so pack your warmest layers for a day trip there.
notes.nov: Gulmarg nights fall below freezing from November, and Srinagar nights come close to it. Gulmarg is much colder than Srinagar, so pack your warmest layers for a day trip there.
notes.mar: Gulmarg nights are still below freezing in March. Gulmarg is much colder than Srinagar, so pack your warmest layers for a day trip there.

places.name: Ladakh (Leh)
places.note: These are IMD's averages for Leh town, at about 3,500 m. Khardung La, Pangong and Tso Moriri are much higher and far colder, so carry a warm jacket even in July. The sun is very strong: wear sunglasses and sunscreen.

source.label: IMD averages for Leh, as tabled on Wikipedia

more: Manali packing list (for the Manali–Leh road)

places.name: Darjeeling
places.note: Tiger Hill at dawn is colder than the town, so wear your warmest layers for the sunrise.

source.label: IMD averages (1991–2020), as tabled on Wikipedia

snow_note.dec: Rare in Darjeeling town. Sandakphu, higher up, gets snow most winters
snow_note.jan: Rare in Darjeeling town. Sandakphu, higher up, gets snow most winters
snow_note.feb: Rare in Darjeeling town. Sandakphu, higher up, gets snow most winters

places.name: Ooty
places.note: Days are mild, but mornings and nights can fall to near 0 °C.

source.label: IMD averages (1991–2020), as tabled on Wikipedia

snow_note.dec: No snow, but you may see ground frost on cold mornings
snow_note.jan: No snow, but you may see ground frost on cold mornings

notes.oct: October is Ooty's wettest month and November is wet too, so pack rain gear. Mornings and nights are cool.
notes.nov: October is Ooty's wettest month and November is wet too, so pack rain gear. Mornings and nights are cool.

places.name: Coorg
places.note: Warm in the sun by day, cool at night and misty in the early morning.

source.label: IMD averages (1981–2010), as tabled on Wikipedia

places.name: Meghalaya (Shillong, Cherrapunji)
places.note: Days are cool and short, and nights in Shillong can fall near freezing.

source.label: IMD averages (1991–2020), as tabled on Wikipedia

snow_note.dec: No snow, but frost is possible on the coldest mornings
snow_note.jan: No snow, but frost is possible on the coldest mornings

places.name: Rishikesh
places.note: These are IMD's numbers for Dehradun, the nearest station. Nights in riverside camps can drop close to 5 °C, so bring warm sleepwear.

source.label: IMD Dehradun climate table (1991–2020)

places.name: Auli
places.note: These are IMD's numbers for Joshimath, about 700–1,100 m lower than Auli. Auli itself is several degrees colder and often below freezing at night.

source.label: IMD climate normals for Joshimath (1971–2000), as tabled on Wikipedia

snow_note.dec: Possible on the slopes, not certain

places.name: Nainital
places.note: These are IMD's numbers for Mukteshwar, a little higher than Nainital. Nights by the lake are close to freezing.

source.label: IMD climate normals for Mukteshwar (1991–2020), as tabled on Wikipedia

places.name: Mussoorie
places.note: Sunny days are mild, but evenings on the ridge are cold and windy.

source.label: IMD climate normals for Mussoorie (1971–2000), as tabled on Wikipedia

places.name: Jim Corbett
places.note: These are IMD's numbers for Pantnagar, in the plains. Early-morning safaris in an open jeep feel much colder than the number.

source.label: IMD climate normals for Pantnagar (1991–2020), as tabled on Wikipedia

places.name: Hampi
places.note: Hot in the sun among the rocks by midday, pleasant in the early morning and evening. Cover shoulders and knees for temples.

source.label: IMD averages for Ballari (1981–2010), as tabled on Wikipedia

places.name: Ranthambore
places.note: Sunny days and cold mornings. A 7 AM safari in an open jeep feels much colder than the number.

source.label: IMD averages for Sawai Madhopur (1991–2020), as tabled on Wikipedia

places.name: Pondicherry
places.note: Warm and humid all winter. December is the last month of the northeast monsoon, with heavy showers on some days, so carry a rain jacket or umbrella.

source.label: IMD averages for Pondicherry airport (1991–2020), as tabled on Wikipedia

places.name: Varanasi
places.note: Dense fog is common from late December to January. Mornings and nights by the river feel cold.

source.label: IMD averages (1991–2020), as tabled on Wikipedia

places.name: Udaipur
places.note: Afternoons are pleasant, but it gets about 17 °C colder after dark. Carry a warm jacket for the evenings.

source.label: IMD Udaipur averages (1981–2010)

places.name: Jaisalmer
places.note: Desert days are warm, but it gets about 15 °C colder after dark, and a night in a dune camp is colder still. Carry a warm jacket.

source.label: IMD Jaisalmer averages (1981–2010)

places.name: Rann of Kutch (Bhuj)
places.note: Sunny days and cold nights. The open White Rann feels colder in the wind at sunset and under the full moon, and the glare off the salt is strong.

source.label: IMD Bhuj averages (1981–2010)

places.name: Jaipur
places.note: Mornings are the coldest, around 7–8 AM. A few nights each winter drop to 2–3 °C.

source.label: IMD climate of Jaipur

places.name: Goa
places.note: Warm and dry, with pleasant evenings. Wear swimwear at the beach and pool only, with a shirt or kaftan over it in town.

source.label: IMD averages for Goa

notes.oct: October still gets heavy showers, about 156 mm in the month, so pack for rain as well as sun. Wear swimwear at the beach and pool only, with a shirt or kaftan over it in town.

places.name: Kerala
places.note: The coast is hot, but Munnar in the tea hills has cold nights, and some winters touch 0 °C.

source.label: IMD averages (1991–2020) for the coast; tea research station records for Munnar, January 2026, as given in our Kerala guide

places.name: Andaman
places.note: It never gets cold, so you won't need woollens. Storms can come in December, so keep a spare day.

source.label: IMD Port Blair station and WMO normals

places.name: Bhutan

snow.dec: Possible on the high passes (Dochula, Chele La), not certain in the towns
snow.jan: Possible on the high passes (Dochula, Chele La), not certain in the towns

places.note: Days are sunny and nights are freezing in Paro, Thimphu and Bumthang. Punakha is the warm one. Dress in layers you can take off at noon.

source.label: NCHM averages, as tabled on Wikipedia

places.name: Dubai
places.note: Cover your shoulders and midriff in public places, and keep swimwear for the beach and pool. Take a warmer jacket for evening desert trips in winter.

source.label: UAE National Center of Meteorology averages on the WMO's World Weather Information Service

places.name: Thailand
places.note: The Grand Palace doesn't allow sleeveless, short or see-through tops. Malls, buses and flights are cold, so carry one light layer.

source.label: Thai Meteorological Department averages on the WMO's World Weather Information Service

places.name: Bali
places.note: Cover your shoulders and knees at temples. Some, like Besakih, require a sarong and sash.

source.label: BMKG averages for Denpasar on the WMO's World Weather Information Service

places.name: Vietnam
places.note: Pack for two climates: the north is cool, with lows of about 10 °C in cold spells, and the south is hot.

source.label: Viet Nam Meteorological and Hydrological Administration averages (1991–2020) on the WMO's World Weather Information Service

places.name: Maldives
places.note: Resorts are relaxed, but cover your shoulders and knees in Malé and on local islands. Take one light layer for the flight.

source.label: Maldives Meteorological Service averages on the WMO's World Weather Information Service

places.name: Sri Lanka
places.note: No shorts or sleeveless tops at the Temple of the Tooth in Kandy. Take a warm layer for Nuwara Eliya and the hill train.

source.label: National Meteorological Centre averages on the WMO's World Weather Information Service

places.name: Nepal
places.note: Cover your shoulders and knees at temples, and wear shoes that slip off easily. Hill viewpoints like Nagarkot and Sarangkot are colder at sunrise.

source.label: Nepal Department of Hydrology and Meteorology averages (1991–2020), as tabled on Wikipedia

places.name: Tokyo
places.note: Winter in Japan is cold but mostly dry and sunny. Shops and trains are heated, so wear layers you can take off.

source.label: Japan Meteorological Agency averages (1991–2020), as in our Japan trip guide

places.name: Kyoto
places.note: Winter in Japan is cold but mostly dry and sunny. Shops and trains are heated, so wear layers you can take off.

source.label: Japan Meteorological Agency averages (1991–2020), as in our Japan trip guide

places.name: Paris
places.note: Paris is cold and damp. Wind and rain make it feel colder than the number.

source.label: MeteoSwiss, Météo-France and the Italian Air Force Meteorological Service averages, published by the World Meteorological Organization, as in our Europe trip guide

places.name: Rome
places.note: Rome is the mildest in winter, but its nights are still about 3 to 4 °C in December and January.

source.label: MeteoSwiss, Météo-France and the Italian Air Force Meteorological Service averages, published by the World Meteorological Organization, as in our Europe trip guide

places.name: Zurich
places.note: Zurich is the coldest of the three, and the Alps are colder still. Days are short.

source.label: MeteoSwiss, Météo-France and the Italian Air Force Meteorological Service averages, published by the World Meteorological Organization, as in our Europe trip guide

places.name: Seoul
places.note: Indoors is heated, so wear layers you can take off. Wind makes Seoul feel colder than the number.

source.label: Korea Meteorological Administration averages (1991–2020) for Seoul, Busan and Jeju, published on the WMO's World Weather Information Service, as in our South Korea guide

places.name: Singapore
places.note: Malls, the MRT and cinemas are cold, so carry one light layer. Carry an umbrella or a poncho.

source.label: Meteorological Service Singapore long-term averages (1991–2020) at Changi, as in our Singapore guide

places.name: Hong Kong
places.note: December evenings are cool: pack a light jacket or sweater, and a warmer layer for Victoria Peak and windy ferry rides.

source.label: Hong Kong Observatory monthly meteorological normals (1991–2020), as in our Hong Kong guide

places.name: Istanbul and Cappadocia
places.note: December is Istanbul's wettest month: pack warm, waterproof clothes. Cappadocia drops below freezing at night.

source.label: Turkish State Meteorological Service averages for Istanbul and Nevşehir on the WMO's World Weather Information Service, as in our Turkey guide

places.name: Baku
places.note: December in Baku is cool, not snowy. For snow, go up to the mountains around Shahdag or Gabala.

source.label: Azerbaijan National Hydrometeorological Service averages for Baku on the WMO's World Weather Information Service, as in our Azerbaijan guide

places.name: Almaty
places.note: Pack thermals, a padded jacket and boots with a good grip. Winter precipitation here falls as rain or snow.

source.label: Kazhydromet averages for Almaty on the WMO's World Weather Information Service, as in our Kazakhstan guide

snow.dec: Snow some days in December, says our Kazakhstan guide

places.name: Oman
places.note: May to September is very hot in the north, so plan sightseeing for early morning. Salalah is green and cool in its July and August monsoon.

source.label: Oman Directorate General of Meteorology averages for Muscat, Nizwa and Salalah on the WMO's World Weather Information Service, as in our Oman guide

places.name: Tashkent and Samarkand
places.note: Summer is hot and dry, so start early and rest at midday. Winter nights are near freezing.

source.label: Uzhydromet averages for Tashkent and Samarkand on the WMO's World Weather Information Service, as in our Uzbekistan guide

places.name: Manila
places.note: It's warm all year. Rain starts in May and peaks in July and August, so carry a poncho then.

source.label: PAGASA averages for Metro Manila on the WMO's World Weather Information Service, as in our Philippines guide

places.name: Siem Reap
places.note: March to May is the hottest time: visit the temples at sunrise and rest at midday.

source.label: Cambodia Ministry of Water Resources and Meteorology averages for Siem Reap and Phnom Penh on the WMO's World Weather Information Service, as in our Cambodia guide

places.name: Sydney and Melbourne
places.note: Seasons are the reverse of India's. Winter (June to August) is cool, not freezing, in Sydney and Melbourne.

source.label: Australian Bureau of Meteorology averages for Sydney and Melbourne on the WMO's World Weather Information Service, as in our Australia guide

places.name: Auckland
places.note: Seasons are the reverse of India's. July is Auckland's wettest month, and the colder south is colder still.

source.label: MetService (New Zealand) averages (1981–2010) for Auckland on the WMO's World Weather Information Service, as in our New Zealand guide

places.name: Toronto
places.note: Winter here is long and cold. Wear thermals, a padded jacket, gloves and a cap.

source.label: Meteorological Service of Canada (Environment and Climate Change Canada) averages (1971–2000) for Toronto on the WMO's World Weather Information Service, as in our Canada guide

snow.jan: Snow in January, says our Canada guide

places.name: Vancouver
places.note: Winters are mild but wet, so a waterproof jacket matters more than a heavy coat.

source.label: Meteorological Service of Canada (Environment and Climate Change Canada) averages (1971–2000) for Vancouver on the WMO's World Weather Information Service, as in our Canada guide

places.name: Nairobi and Masai Mara
places.note: Nights are cool in Nairobi and the Mara, about 9 to 13 °C, so carry a warm layer. The coast is hot all year.

source.label: Kenya Meteorological Department averages for Nairobi, Narok and Mombasa on the WMO's World Weather Information Service, as in our Kenya safari guide

places.name: New York
places.note: January is the coldest month. Pack thermals, a padded coat, gloves and warm, grippy shoes for December to February.

source.label: US National Weather Service averages (1981–2010) for New York on the WMO's World Weather Information Service, as in our USA guide

places.name: Cairo, Luxor and Hurghada
places.note: Winter nights are cool, about 6 to 8 °C in Luxor in December and January, so carry a warm layer for early starts. Summer is very hot.

source.label: Egyptian Meteorological Authority averages for Cairo, Luxor and Hurghada on the WMO's World Weather Information Service, as in our Egypt guide

places.name: London and Edinburgh
places.note: December is cold and dark early. Edinburgh is colder and windier, around freezing at night.

source.label: Met Office averages for London and Edinburgh on the WMO's World Weather Information Service, as in our UK guide
